composition_parti.rule: Composition is generated by the plan module and the porch, not by an applied classical or picturesque parti: the street facade is near-symmetrical about the porch/gable centreline (two openings -- a door and a window -- or three on a double shotgun), while the depth of the house is a simple additive repetition of the room module (own proportional_system.bay_rhythm and symmetry: near-symmetrical).
composition_parti.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'additive-vernacular... imposed symmetry or a designed picturesque irregularity are both outside the type' from tuscan-vernacular, a contour-following farmhouse rule. This node's own proportional_system states near-symmetry IS present, specifically at the street face.

variants.note: Own defining_characteristics #3: 'Gable end turned to the street, with a full-width porch under or attached to the front gable.'
The opposite of the type's most basic diagnostic; own distinguished_from vs massing:gable-front confirms the gable-to-street move is definitional.

roof_form.rule: Gable end turned to the street, ridge running front-to-back over the full depth of the house.
roof_form.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'hip' from french-colonial-american -- a hipped roof has no gable end at all, directly contradicting the node's own name-giving diagnostic.

roof_pitch.rule: Roof pitch 6:12 to 10:12, front-gabled (own typical_ratios); the camelback rear section rises 1.5-2 storeys behind the single-storey street reading.
roof_pitch.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 40-50 degree hipped-roof figure from french-colonial-american, expressed in degrees rather than this corpus's rise_in_12 convention and attached to the wrong roof form entirely.

variants.note: A later, and now more common, re-roofing over the same wood-frame structure.
A heavy masonry-compatible roofing system with no fit to the light wood frame this type actually uses (construction_type, below).

roof_material.rule: Wood shingle historically, corrugated or standing-seam metal increasingly from the later 19th century onward -- both light roofing systems consistent with a light wood frame.
roof_material.note: CASCADE FIX (partial inference). Own text does not state a roofing material directly, so this is a judgment call grounded in construction_type (below, wood frame) rather than a documented fact; what IS certain and stated here as fact is that clay-tile-barrel, inherited from mediterranean-vernacular, is wrong -- that is a heavy masonry-era Mediterranean roofing system with no basis in this type's own wood-frame, catalogue-millwork construction.

eave_condition.rule: A plain boxed or open eave with a modest wood overhang -- not the corbelled masonry genoise courses of the ancestor binding, which presuppose a load-bearing masonry wall this type does not have (construction_type, below).
eave_condition.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'genoise-corbelled-tile-courses' from french-provincial-farmhouse, a masonry cornice device (corbelled canal tile bedded in mortar) with no application to a wood-frame house. Own text does not describe eave detail directly, so the replacement is held at low confidence.

chimney.rule_append: In the single-file shotgun plan, the 'paired rooms' the ancestor rule describes are the successive rooms of the front-to-back enfilade: the chimney sits on the partition wall shared by two adjoining rooms, most often the front two, and never on the street gable itself, which carries the type's entire ornamental identity (own defining_characteristics #6) rather than a flue.

height_proportion.rule: One storey throughout for the full length of the house is the norm; the sole exception is the camelback, which raises a second storey over the rear rooms only, beginning at least two rooms back from the front wall so the street elevation still reads as single-storey (own hard constraint c05, soft).

variants.note: Contradicted by the node's own construction description (cypress/pine mill-sawn frame, machine-cut nails); the type builds nothing load-bearing in masonry.

construction_type.rule: Mill-sawn cypress and pine, light wood frame, machine-cut nails and catalogue millwork (own long description, third paragraph: 'Mill-sawn cypress and pine, machine-cut nails and catalogue millwork made it fast and cheap to build'); not masonry construction of any kind.
construction_type.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'solid-masonry-two-wythe' from american-colonial, flatly contradicted by the node's own construction description.

wall_thickness_masonry.rule: There is no masonry wall; the structure is a light wood frame (construction_type, already specified).
wall_thickness_masonry.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 500-700 mm rubble-wall thickness figure from french-provincial-farmhouse, meaningless against a wood-frame wall.

primary_cladding.rule: Horizontal wood weatherboard is the norm; board-and-batten also occurs (own exemplar: the 1897 Ocean Park, Santa Monica example is described as 'board-and-batten'). Never masonry or a masonry veneer.
primary_cladding.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'rubble-limestone-lime-render' from french-provincial-farmhouse, a load-bearing rural masonry cladding with no basis in this type's own wood-frame construction.

secondary_cladding.rule: One cladding material runs over the whole building; there is no secondary or accent cladding distinguishing one elevation from another, unlike the essentage convention of an unrelated half-timber/masonry building culture.
secondary_cladding.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'essentage-slate-or-split-shingle-hung' from norman-vernacular, a rain-shielding treatment specific to a half-timbered Norman wall system this type does not share.

foundation_expression.rule: Raised on brick or cypress piers with an open crawl space beneath, 18-36 in above grade (own diagnostic tell; consistent with grade_relationship, already resolving correctly); never a podium or a stepped masonry base of any kind.
foundation_expression.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'high-podium-frontal-stair' from roman-classical -- a temple foundation with no relationship to a light, piered wood-frame cottage.

reveal_masonry.rule: There is no masonry wall to set an opening into (construction_type, already specified); window_head_masonry is forbidden below for the same reason.
reveal_masonry.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 12-24 in masonry reveal-depth figure from mediterranean-vernacular.

cornice.rule: No applied classical cornice occurs; ornament in this type is concentrated entirely on the street gable and porch in whatever millwork the current catalogue offered (own defining_characteristics #6), not in a classical crown moulding.
cornice.note: Restates the inherited conclusion (forbidden, from mediterranean-vernacular) on this node's own ground -- that source held it at low confidence as an inference; this node's own text states the gable/porch-concentration rule directly.

frieze.rule: No classical frieze band occurs, for the same reason as cornice: ornament in this type is concentrated on the gable and porch millwork, not an applied entablature band (own defining_characteristics #6).
frieze.note: Restates the inherited conclusion (forbidden, from mediterranean-vernacular) on this node's own ground, replacing that source's low-confidence inference with a direct citation.

window_type.rule: Double-hung wood sash, commonly 1/1 or 2/2 panes by the type's later catalogue-millwork floruit (per the bound sash-light pack's own note on this node: 'commonly large 1/1 or 2/2 panes by that date'); not a French casement.
window_type.note: Own text does not state sash type directly; grounded in the node's already-bound sash-light pack note and its own description of an 1880s-1890s Italianate/Eastlake catalogue-millwork era.

window_head_masonry.rule: There is no masonry opening head; window_head_wood is the only applicable slot given the wood-frame construction already specified.
window_head_masonry.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a relieving-arch rule for openings wider than 1.2 m from french-provincial-farmhouse, meaningless in a wood-frame wall.

window_grouping_rule.rule: The street facade carries two openings only -- a door and a window -- under the gable, or three on a double shotgun; the side elevation carries one window per room at even spacing, the plan module made visible on the wall (own proportional_system.bay_rhythm).
window_grouping_rule.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'irregular and functional... no governing datum' from french-provincial-farmhouse -- true of that farmhouse's room-by-room fenestration but the opposite of this type's own tightly specified, near-symmetrical street opening count.

shutter.rule_append: Applies per window (and at the single entry door where fitted); the type's own street facade carries at most one door and one window, not the paired French-casement leaves the ancestor rule's leaf-width logic assumes (entry_door, already specified).

entry_door.rule: A single door leaf, paired with a single window, is the entire street-facade opening count in the standard case (own diagnostic tell: 'Front facade of one or two openings only, a door and a window, under a gable').
entry_door.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'french-casement-pair' from french-colonial-american -- a raised-plantation-house device directly contradicted by the node's own diagnostic tell about the street facade carrying at most a door and a window.

door_surround.rule: Ornament is essentially absent at the door surround itself -- a plain wood casing -- consistent with own defining_characteristics #6: ornament in this type is concentrated on the gable and porch millwork as a whole, not on a dressed masonry door surround, which this wood-frame type does not build.
door_surround.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'dressed stone at the door surround' and 'genoise courses' from french-provincial-farmhouse -- both masonry-specific devices with no basis in this type's wood-frame construction (construction_type, already specified).

variants.note: Would break the street gable, the type's entire ornamental identity, and cannot fit the 12-16 ft overall width (own hard constraint c02).

garage_strategy.rule: Where provided at all, the car is accommodated at the rear of the narrow, deep lot -- a detached carport or single garage reached from a rear alley or lane where one exists -- never as a volume attached to or breaking the street gable. On the narrowest historic lots (12-16 ft, own hard constraint c02) no garage is provided at all and on-street parking is the norm.
garage_strategy.note: No historical precedent exists for this slot. Grounded in the node's own revival_periods note describing an active contemporary practice ('small-lot infill and cottage-court type... its 14-foot width... front-porch social logic') where lot narrowness is exactly the operative constraint, and in own hard constraint c02.

porch_type.rule: A full-width porch on the street elevation only -- never wrapping to the side elevations, which face directly onto the neighbouring lot's identical porch a few feet away (own diagnostic tells: porch full width; rows of identical units at 3-6 ft spacings). At least 5 ft deep (own hard constraint c04).
porch_type.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a galerie 'wrapping two to four sides' from french-colonial-american/creole-cottage-vernacular -- appropriate to a broadside Creole cottage on an open lot, wrong for a one-room-wide house on a narrow subdivided lot with only 4-8 ft of side yard.

porch_depth.rule: Porch depth at least 5 ft, 6-8 ft preferred (own hard constraint c04), full width, floor raised 18-36 in above grade on piers.
porch_depth.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved an 8-14 ft galerie depth figure appropriate to a raised plantation house; this node's own typical_ratios and hard constraint c04 give a shallower 5-8 ft porch.

porch_support.rule: Plain wood posts -- turned, chamfered, or in higher-style examples bracketed with Eastlake or Italianate millwork -- not the light iron-rod French colonnette of the plantation-house tradition (own long description: ornament 'absorbed... Italianate brackets, Eastlake spindlework, Queen Anne gable shingles... concentrated on the street gable and the porch').
porch_support.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'colonnette-light, iron-rod-or-bracket-no-post' from french-colonial-american, a plantation-gallery support system rather than this type's own catalogue-millwork porch post.

steps_and_stoop.rule: A short, unenclosed flight of wood steps rises the 18-36 in from grade to the porch floor (grade_relationship); there is no basement or raised principal storey to stair up to beyond the porch itself.

entry_sequence.rule: From the front door an unbroken sightline runs through every intervening doorway to the back door -- across 3-5 rooms -- the type's single most distinctive diagnostic tell (own diagnostic tells #1), and the opposite of a sequence that bypasses any working or service floor.
entry_sequence.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved an exterior stair 'bypassing the stalla' from tuscan-vernacular -- a two-storey Italian farmhouse device (ground-floor animal stable, exterior stair to the family's living floor) with no application to this one-storey, stalla-less type.

ceiling_height_rule.rule: Ceiling height minimum 10 ft (11-12 typical) -- the section, not applied ornament, is the cooling system: a transom over every interior door and operable windows on both side walls of every room (own hard constraint c03).
ceiling_height_rule.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 6.9-8.2 ft 'low, dark and heavily beamed' Norman farmhouse storey height -- nearly the opposite of this type's unusually tall room, which the node's own long description states directly: 'the ceilings are ten to twelve feet so the volume feels far larger than the fourteen-foot width.'

interior_door.rule: Every interior door carries an operable transom above it (own hard constraint c03), consistent with the bound sash-light pack's transom-glazing rule; doors are simple single-leaf, catalogue-stock, and aligned on the house's single longitudinal axis (own hard constraint c01).

floor_material.rule: A wood floor on joists spans between the piers (foundation_expression, above); there is no earth or masonry floor of any kind in a raised, piered building.
floor_material.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'beaten-earth... later terracotta tomettes' from norman-vernacular, a ground-bearing rural French floor system with no relevance to a wood floor framed over an open, raised crawl space.

circulation_parti.rule: A single file of rooms, one room wide, opening directly into the next in an enfilade with no hallway -- typically parlour, bedroom, bedroom, kitchen in sequence -- every door aligned on one longitudinal axis within 3 in, front door to rear (own hard constraint c01, own defining_characteristics #1-2). Reaching the rearmost room means passing through every other room.
circulation_parti.note: CASCADE FIX. The inherited creole-cottage-vernacular extends binding is architecturally close (also hall-less, room-to-room) but describes that cottage's own broadside four-room plan, and its own appended clause already (correctly) flags the shotgun as 'a genuinely different, later type' -- so this node needs its own full statement rather than an extension of a base built for a different plan geometry.

hearth_position.rule: Where documented, a fireplace sits on the partition wall between two adjoining rooms, following chimney (above), serving both; not a gable-wall hearth, which would put the flue on the ornamented street face or the plain rear wall rather than the working spine of the plan.
hearth_position.note: CASCADE FIX. Own text does not describe hearth position explicitly; this follows from chimney (already correctly resolving from the real ancestor creole-cottage-vernacular), replacing a Norman gable-wall/bread-oven hearth rule with no basis in this construction.

stair_position.rule: The standard one-storey shotgun has no stair. In the camelback variant, a single interior stair rises to the raised rear rooms only, beginning at least two rooms back from the front wall (own hard constraint c05); there is no exterior stair to a piano nobile or a working ground floor of the Mediterranean farmhouse kind.
stair_position.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved an exterior stair 'bypassing the stalla' from tuscan-vernacular.

public_private_gradient.rule: There is effectively no privacy gradient of the hallway kind: reaching the rearmost room (kitchen) means passing directly through every intervening room, public and private alike (own long description: 'reaching the last room means passing through every private space in the house'). Public life happens on the porch and in the yard, not through a graded sequence of interior rooms.

room_adjacency_overrides.rule: Rooms are strung front to back in a fixed linear sequence, typically parlour, bedroom, bedroom, kitchen (own long description); each room is adjacent only to the room immediately in front of and behind it, never side-by-side to a room it does not open into, since the house is one room wide throughout.

rules.statement: Rooms are strung front to back in a fixed linear sequence -- typically parlour, bedroom, bedroom, kitchen -- and each room is adjacent only to the room immediately in front of and behind it.
rules.why: The house is one room wide throughout, so there is no side-by-side adjacency to have. The universal records assume a room can have neighbours on more than one side; this says it cannot.

service_zone_strategy.rule: There is no separate service zone or floor; the kitchen is simply the rearmost room in the enfilade sequence (own long description: 'parlour, bedroom, bedroom, kitchen in sequence'), reached by passing through every other room, not a subordinated wing or a stabled ground floor.
service_zone_strategy.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a stalla (ground-floor animal-stabling) rule from tuscan-vernacular.

depth_and_pile.rule_append: Concretely: depth is built by repeating an 11-14 ft square room module 3 to 5 times to a total depth of 40-70 ft (own typical_ratios); width is fixed at 12-16 ft overall (own hard constraint c02) and never absorbs a second pile.

daylight_strategy.rule_append: Concretely: every room needs operable openings on its two long (side) walls, and every interior door needs an operable transom, so that opening the front and back doors on a hot night turns the whole depth of the house into a single ventilation duct (own hard constraint c03, own long description).

street_relationship.rule: The street gable and its porch are the house's entire public face and carry essentially all of its ornament -- Italianate brackets, Eastlake spindlework, Queen Anne shingling, whatever the current millwork catalogue offered (own long description, third and fourth paragraphs) -- the opposite of a blank domestic street face.
street_relationship.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved 'blank-plain-domestic-exterior... to the point of blankness' from roman-classical, directly contradicted by this node's own repeated emphasis on the street gable as the concentrated site of ornament.

setback_rule.rule: Lot frontage 25-32 ft (the New Orleans standard 30 x 120 ft lot), with 4-8 ft of side yard; rows of identical units commonly sit at 3-6 ft spacings, sharing a rhythm but not a party wall (own typical_ratios, own diagnostic tells).

orientation_rule.rule: Orientation is set by the ventilation axis, not by a fixed compass-bound shading rule: front and rear doors align on one axis (own hard constraint c01) so that opening both on a hot night draws air the full depth of the house. Where lot and street geometry allow a choice, the long axis is set to catch the prevailing summer breeze, but the type's own governing rule is the door alignment itself.
orientation_rule.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a 5%-glazed-northwest-wall mistral-avoidance rule from french-provincial-farmhouse -- a Rhone valley wind-shading device with no relationship to this type's own, textually stated, door-alignment ventilation strategy.

outbuilding_types.rule: The narrow, deep urban lot (own typical_ratios: 25-32 ft frontage, 4-8 ft side yard) leaves little room for outbuildings; where one occurs it is a small utility shed at the rear property line, not a freestanding agricultural structure of any scale.
outbuilding_types.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a colombaia (Tuscan dovecote tower) rule from tuscan-vernacular, an agricultural-estate outbuilding with no application to a subdivided urban rental lot.

fence_wall.rule: Where a fence occurs it is a simple wood picket or board fence along the narrow side yard (own typical_ratios: 4-8 ft) or the rear property line; there is no hedged or walled orchard enclosure of the rural farmstead kind.
fence_wall.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a hedged/walled apple-orchard enclosure rule from norman-vernacular, a dispersed rural farmstead device with no relationship to a dense urban rental row.

landscape_idiom.rule: The house is inseparable from the street, not from working agricultural ground: rows of identical porches face one another across a narrow yard a few feet away, and the porch itself -- not a garden -- is the type's one designed outdoor social space (own long description, final paragraph).
landscape_idiom.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved an agricultural terracing/aia landscape idiom from mediterranean-vernacular.

grade_relationship.rule_append: The 'full masonry service storey on the plantation house' option the ancestor rule describes does not occur in this type: the only foundation is brick or cypress piers with an open crawl space beneath (own diagnostic tells), and the house floor sits at the same raised level (18-36 in) as the porch.
